t: Shanghai plunge: S&P 500 −3.5%, Dow −416
how: The largest Dow point loss since 2001; VIX from 11 to 18. The index lost 5.9% in all and was at a new high by mid-April.

t: Bear Stearns mortgage fund freezes redemptions
how: April loss restated from 6.6% to 19%. S&P 500 −1.8% that day. Lenders seized collateral two weeks later.

t: Bear Stearns: its two funds are nearly worthless
how: S&P 500 flat; the Dow touched 14,000 intraday for the first time. The funds filed for bankruptcy on 31 July.

t: Dow closes above 14,000; transports peak
how: S&P 500 record close of 1,553.08. Small companies had peaked on 13 July. Neither they nor the transports confirmed the October high.

t: BNP Paribas freezes three funds; ECB lends about €95bn
how: S&P 500 −3.0%, Dow −387. Bank-to-bank rates jumped. Quant funds had been forced to sell all week.

t: Fed cuts its discount rate by 0.50 point
how: S&P 500 +2.5%, Dow +233, the day after an intraday low 11.7% below the July high. The policy rate was left at 5.25%.

t: First rate cut: 0.50 point to 4.75%
how: S&P 500 +2.9%, Dow +336. The index made its record three weeks later and fell 55% from this day’s close to the low.

t: S&P 500 record close: 1,565.15
how: VIX 16.1. Transports were 8.4% and financials 6.5% below their highs. The index fell 56.8% from here in 355 sessions.

t: Fed cuts to 4.50%, calls risks roughly balanced
how: S&P 500 +1.2% to within 1.0% of the high. Next day a Citigroup downgrade sent it down 2.6%.

t: First close 10% below the peak: 1,407.22
how: S&P 500 −2.3%, 33 sessions after the peak. VIX had peaked at 31.1 on 12 November, above its August high.

t: Fed’s Kohn promises flexible policy: S&P 500 +2.9%
how: Dow +331. Bernanke spoke the next day. The index rose 7.7% in two weeks, to 3.1% below the high.

t: Fed cuts only 0.25 point: S&P 500 −2.5%
how: Dow −294. The Fed’s staff forecast no recession that day; the recession was later dated to this month.

t: Emergency cut of 0.75 point to 3.50%
how: After a global rout on a US holiday. Dow down 464 intraday, closed −128. Next day’s intraday low was 18.9% below the peak.

t: Fed offers $200bn of Treasuries against mortgage bonds
how: S&P 500 +3.7%, Dow +417, the day after a closing low of 1,273.37. Bear Stearns failed anyway within the week.

t: JPMorgan buys Bear Stearns at $2 a share
how: Agreed on Sunday 16 March with Fed support. Intraday low 1,256.98; S&P 500 closed −0.9%. VIX 32.2, its high for the first half.

t: Fed cuts 0.75 point to 2.25%: S&P 500 +4.2%
how: Dow +420. Start of a two-month rally of 12.0% from the 10 March close.

t: Rally high: S&P 500 1,426.63
how: 8.9% below the record and just under a falling 200-day average. VIX 17.0. Energy and materials shares peaked the next day.

t: S&P 500 first closes 20% below its peak
how: 1,244.69, nine months after the high. The Dow had crossed the same line on 27 June.

t: Oil record $147.27; IndyMac bank fails
how: S&P 500 −1.1%. Worry turned to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; the summer low came on 15 July at 1,214.91.

t: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac taken over by the government
how: Announced on Sunday 7 September. S&P 500 +2.1%, then −3.4% the next day.

t: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy
how: S&P 500 −4.7%, Dow −504. Merrill Lynch was sold to Bank of America the same weekend.

t: AIG rescued with $85bn; a money fund breaks the buck
how: S&P 500 +1.8%, then −4.7% on 17 September as prime money funds lost $349bn in a week.

t: Short-selling ban on financials; bank rescue proposed
how: S&P 500 +4.0% after +4.3% the day before. The gains were gone by 29 September.

t: House rejects the rescue plan: S&P 500 −8.8%
how: Dow −777.68, a record point loss. VIX 46.7. The index regained 5.4% the next day.

t: Rescue plan (TARP) passes and is sold
how: S&P 500 −1.4% on the day, then −18.2% over the next five sessions.

t: Crash-week low: 839.80 intraday on record volume
how: Close 899.22. Bank-to-bank stress (TED spread) at a record 4.58. Volume and new lows peaked here, five months before the final low.

t: Governments put capital into banks: S&P 500 +11.6%
how: Dow +936, the largest one-day gains since at least 1950. Two days later the S&P 500 fell 9.0%.

t: VIX intraday record: 89.53
how: S&P 500 −3.5% as world markets fell about 10%. The closing low of 848.92 came on 27 October, then +10.8% on 28 October.

t: Election-day high: S&P 500 1,005.75
how: +4.1% on the day, +18.5% from 27 October. The index then lost 25.2% in twelve sessions.

t: S&P 500 752.44; VIX closes at a record 80.86
how: −6.7% after −6.1%. Citigroup −26%. Technology, Nasdaq 100, emerging markets and high-yield bonds made their lows here.

t: Citigroup rescued: $306bn of assets guaranteed
how: Agreed on Sunday 23 November. S&P 500 +6.5% after +6.3% on Friday: the Dow’s largest two-day gain since 1987.

t: Fed to buy $600bn of agency debt and mortgage bonds
how: S&P 500 +0.7%. Mortgage rates fell from 6.04% to 5.10% by year-end, the first easing to reach borrowers.

t: NBER: recession began in December 2007
how: S&P 500 −8.9%, financials −17%. The announcement came twelve months after the recession started.

t: Fed cuts to 0–0.25%
how: S&P 500 +5.1%. The last rate cut available; the index was still 35% above its eventual low.

t: Rally high: S&P 500 934.70
how: Up 24.2% from 20 November without one close above the 200-day average. The index fell 27.6% from here.

t: Treasury’s bank plan lacks detail: S&P 500 −4.9%
how: A week later the fiscal stimulus was signed and the index fell 4.6% that day.

t: Record 70.3% of individual investors bearish
how: S&P 500 −4.3% as General Motors’ auditors doubted its survival. The intraday low of 666.79 came the next day.

t: Bear-market low: S&P 500 676.53
how: −1.0% on the day on volume a third below October’s. VIX 49.7 against 80.9 in November; the Nasdaq 100 held its November low.

t: Citigroup says it was profitable in 2009: S&P 500 +6.4%
how: Citigroup +38%. Bernanke spoke the same day about accounting rules. A 90% up-volume day; a second followed on 12 March.

t: Fed adds $750bn of mortgage bonds and $300bn of Treasuries
how: S&P 500 +2.1%. Seventh session after the low; the index was 17% above it.

t: Treasury asset-purchase plan: S&P 500 +7.1%
how: Bank of America +38%. First breadth thrust since 1992 on one published measure. The index was 21.6% above its low and back over its 50-day average.

t: Mark-to-market accounting rules eased; G20 meets
how: S&P 500 +2.9%. Banks could value hard-to-sell assets less harshly.

t: Stress tests: ten banks must raise $74.6bn
how: Released after the close; S&P 500 −1.3% that day and +2.4% the next. The index was 37% above its low.

t: S&P 500 closes above its 200-day average
how: First close above it since December 2007, 58 sessions after the low and 39.4% above it.
